evals.prompt: 我想在香蕉派上对 ResNet50 做 perf profiling，用 generic_ort_runner 跑 30 次迭代，采样 999Hz。板子 IP 是 192.168.1.22，密码 bianbu。
evals.expected_output: Agent follows the perf-profiling phases: (1) resolves 'resnet50' from model registry, downloads if needed. (2) Detects framework as 'ort' from .onnx extension, finds rootfs.tar.gz for chroot mode. (3) Uploads rootfs.tar.gz and model via scp, extracts rootfs, copies model into it. (4) Sets up chroot mounts, runs perf stat + perf record (cpu-clock, -F 999) + perf report + perf annotate via ssh. (5) Downloads perf_stat.txt, perf_report.txt, perf_annotate.txt via scp. (6) Generates summary.md with metrics table.

evals.prompt: 帮我对 ResNet50、MobileNetV2 两个模型做批量 perf profiling，对比热点函数。香蕉派 192.168.1.22，密码 bianbu。
evals.expected_output: Agent profiles both models sequentially using the perf-profiling phases: resolves both models, uploads them, runs perf stat/record/report/annotate for each, downloads results. Generates summary.md comparing top functions, IPC, cycles, and cache miss rates across both models. Identifies shared hot functions as priority fusion targets. Notes cpu-clock event is used for RISC-V.

evals.prompt: 帮我对 Qwen2.5-0.5B-Q4_0.gguf 用 llama.cpp 做 perf profiling，prompt 是 'Hello world'，生成 128 tokens。香蕉派 192.168.1.22。
evals.expected_output: Agent follows perf-profiling phases: (1) resolves 'qwen-0.5b-q4_0' from registry, downloads GGUF. (2) Detects framework as 'llama' from .gguf extension, uses direct mode (no rootfs). (3) Uploads llama-cli binary, shared libs, and model via scp. (4) Runs perf with LD_LIBRARY_PATH, uses runner command 'llama-cli -m <model.gguf> -p "Hello world" -n 128'. (5) Downloads and summarizes results.

evals.prompt: 我从 perf annotate 里看到一段热点汇编，连续的 ld + addw + sw 占了 30% 的采样，这是什么类型的 fusion 候选？还有 mulw + addw 的链式组合占了 25%，这两种哪个收益更大？
evals.expected_output: Agent identifies: (1) ld+addw+sw as load-compute-store (memory-ALU fusion) pattern, (2) mulw+addw as multiply-accumulate chain (MAC fusion) pattern. Explains both are high-value candidates. Compares: MAC fusion likely has higher benefit because multiply has longer latency and MAC is common in CNN kernels. Recommends profiling more models to see if both patterns appear consistently across workloads.
